questionText: A partnership firm having partners X and Y (Firm #15) with capitals of Rs. 680,000 and Rs. 340,000 suffered a net loss of Rs. 58,000 during the year. The deed provides for interest on capital @ 10% p.a. but does not specify whether it is a charge or appropriation. What is the amount of interest on capital allowable?

options.text: Interest will be credited to Current Account only
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Full interest of Rs. 68,000 and Rs. 34,000 will be paid creating further loss

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Company Accounts: Accounting for Share and Debenture Capital (Interest on Capital: Loss Incurred):
No interest on capital will be allowed to any partner

Detailed Analysis:
1. Interest on capital is an appropriation of profit. When the firm incurs a net loss (here Rs. 58,000), no interest on capital can be allowed unless the partnership deed expressly provides that interest on capital is a charge against profits.
Hence Option C is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: Company Apex #8 forfeited 340 shares of Rs. 10 each on which Rs. 7 per share was received. 340 of these shares were reissued as fully paid-up at Rs. 8 per share. What amount is transferred to Capital Reserve Account?

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 2,880 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 2,880
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 680 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 680
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 1,700 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 1,700
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares: Transfer to Capital Reserve.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 2,380 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 2,380
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Company Accounts: Accounting for Share and Debenture Capital (Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares: Transfer to Capital Reserve):
Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 1,700 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 1,700

Detailed Analysis:
1. Forfeited amount on 340 shares = 340 x Rs. 7 = Rs. 2,380.
2. Forfeited amount proportional to 340 reissued shares = 340 x Rs. 7 = Rs. 2,380.
3. Discount allowed on reissue = 340 x (Rs. 10 - Rs. 8) = Rs. 680.
4. Net gain transferred to Capital Reserve = Rs. 2,380 - Rs. 680 = Rs. 1,700.
Hence Option C is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions.
X Itd. Issued 30,000 shares to the public having Face value 100 at 10%
premium. Money is receivable as follows:
Application = 40 (including premium)
Allotment=45
 
First and Final call = Remaining amount
The public applied for 50,000 shares. The company rejected application for
10,000 shares and made a pro rata allotment to the rest of the applicants. A
shareholder applying for 400 shares, didn't pay the allotment and call
money and his allotted shares were forfeited by the company. Later, the
forfeited shares were reissued at 80 each as fully paid.
Amount to be credited to Calls-in Arrears account at the time of forfeiture
is:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Forfeiture of Shares.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Forfeiture of Shares (Company Accounts: Accounting for Share and Debenture Capital):
1. Allotted shares: 400 * (3/4) = 300 shares.
2. Excess application money: (400 - 300) * 40 = Rs. 4,000.
3. Allotment arrears: (300 * 45) - 4,000 = Rs. 9,500.
4. Call arrears: 300 * 25 = Rs. 7,500.
5. Total credited to Calls-in-Arrears = 9,500 + 7,500 = Rs. 17,000.
6. Matches Option C.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
